correctness.rationale: For the specified one-lead, positive-uniform-loss model the tridiagonal Schur complement gives \(b_n=P_{n-1}/P_n\) and exact reflection \(r=(1-h^2b_n)/(1+h^2b_n)\). Odd \(b_n\) is decreasing; even \(\log b_n\) has a unique critical zero by strict negative second derivative, proving the exhaustive 1 versus 0/1/2 positive-root classification. At the even maximum the logarithmic curvature cancels exactly to -(2n+1), proving quartic reflection. The critical-point identity establishes all stated length asymptotics. Direct stationary linear-system and flux checks passed 813 finite instances, not substituted for general proof. The assumptions and normalization are explicit.

value.rationale: The single experimentally meaningful interface hopping bond is a structural bifurcation parameter: above an exact threshold, an even-length uniformly dissipative termination, previously unable to absorb perfectly with a homogeneous interface, acquires two distinct perfect-loss matches. The nondegenerate maximum gives a universal fourth-order reflection tolerance at criticality, and asymptotics quantify the finite-size approach of the critical interface to the homogeneous value. This is a full natural classification, not a renamed single-site example, arbitrary numerical sample, or trivial corollary of the homogeneous-interface prior.
